paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when leaders and people turn against the LORD, everything they were leaning on gets pulled out from under them. Isaiah says the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove "both supply and support" (Isaiah 3:1). Food, water, leaders, the whole org chart, gone. Back in Isaiah 2:22, he already said to stop trusting in man, and chapter 3 shows why.

Notice that the trouble starts at the heart. Isaiah says Jerusalem stumbled "because they spoke and acted against the LORD" (Isaiah 3:8). Then he says they flaunt their sin and don't hide it (Isaiah 3:9). And the LORD does not treat everybody the same here: it will be well with the righteous, and the wicked will be repaid with what their hands have done (Isaiah 3:10-11). So the question for you, friend, is what you are leaning on, and who you are following.

The part that gets me is the LORD's charge against the elders and leaders of His people. Leaders were supposed to guide, and God says they mislead (Isaiah 3:12). He says the plunder of the poor is in their houses, and then asks, "Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?" (Isaiah 3:14-15). That tells me God sees how the weak get treated, and He takes it personally. So I want my ovens ready, my hands clean and my eyes open for the people nobody else notices. And the story isn't over, because Isaiah still has more to say.
